reference.name: chores
reference.context: Canonical reference for outstanding chores for the project. Chores are small actionable items that need to be addressed, but do not take priority over active development work.

chore.synopsis: Rename `TrustData.asset_summary()` loop variables in v3/schema.py to distinct names, silencing mypy loop-variable-reuse errors that were blocking the `pixi run check` gate for the promote_seed refinement plan.

chores.chore: `TrustData.asset_summary()` had six sequential for-loops reusing the variable names `p` and `v` across differently-typed asset lists. mypy narrowed each variable from the first loop's type and rejected later reassignments, producing 8 errors (`assignment` and `attr-defined`) that blocked the `pixi run check` gate. Fix: rebind each loop to a distinct, descriptive name. No behavior change. Pre-plan unblocking commit for plan 3 (`2026-04-23-promote-seed`), outside its §8.2 scope lock but required for its gate to pass.

chore.synopsis: Amendments A-4/A-5/A-6 to firm-config spec per diagnostics §13: tilde expansion on Path fields; required `[user] upn` section; `${user.upn}` post-parse substitution in `diagnostics.audit_log_dir`. Single-commit amendment pass per spec §13.5/§13.6.

chores.chore: The diagnostics-engine spec (§11, §13) specifies audit-log persistence in terms of three `firm.toml` surfaces that do not yet exist: a `[user]` section with a `upn` field, tilde expansion in path resolution, and loader-side `${user.upn}` post-parse substitution in `diagnostics.audit_log_dir`. Because the firm-config spec is the authoritative source for `firm.toml`, the surfaces must be added by amending firm-config (not diagnostics). Three amendments land as a single atomic change set per the asset-summary-loopvar precedent: A-4 extends `_resolve_paths` with `Path.expanduser()` for all Path fields; A-5 adds a `User(BaseModel)` with a non-empty `upn` validator wired into `FirmConfig`; A-6 substitutes `${user.upn}` in `diagnostics.audit_log_dir` prior to expanduser/resolve. Existing test fixtures gain a `[user]` block. Blocks downstream diagnostics-engine plans (plans index 7 and 8) that depend on the new FirmConfig surface.

chore.synopsis: Wrap `_resolve_paths` calls in `load_firm_config` so `OSError`/`RuntimeError` from `Path.expanduser()` and `Path.resolve()` surface as `FirmConfigError`, honoring the §7 exception-contract documented in the firm-config spec.

chores.chore: Surfaced during code review of the A-4/A-5/A-6 amendment pass (chore index 2). `Path.expanduser()` raises `RuntimeError` for unresolvable home prefixes and `Path.resolve()` can raise `OSError` on pathological filesystem states; both currently escape `_resolve_paths` unwrapped, bypassing the `FirmConfigError` contract documented in firm-config spec §7. Production exposure is narrow (the `audit_log_dir` always starts with `~/Crosby and Crosby LLP/...`) but the contract leak is real. Fix: wrap the `_resolve_paths` call in `load_firm_config` in a single try/except that surfaces both as `FirmConfigError`, plus one regression test.

chore.synopsis: Realign diagnostics spec §14.1's cycle-8 summary with §6.9's authoritative cycle definition. §14.1 reads `WARNING/ERROR with approaching-cliff variant`; §6.9 specifies a single WARNING-level `crossed_cliff` rule using `*_hard` thresholds only.

chores.chore: §14.1's plan-boundary table summarizes Cycle 8 as `estate.crossed_cliff — DiagnosticSource.BUSINESS_RULE, WARNING/ERROR with approaching-cliff variant`, but §6.9 (the authoritative cycle definition) specifies only a single WARNING-level rule firing on `>= single_hard` / `>= joint_hard`. The §14.1 wording reads as a pre-split aspirational summary that did not get reconciled when §6.9 was finalized at single-rule scope. The firm config does carry `*_soft` thresholds + `approaching_cliff_ratio`, so an "approaching" variant has surface to consume — but that's a future scope expansion, not a present spec gap. Resolve in one of two directions: (a) drop the WARNING/ERROR + approaching-cliff wording from §14.1 to match §6.9 (minimum-disturbance fix); (b) add a §6.9b for an `estate.approaching_cliff` rule and re-tier `crossed_cliff` to ERROR (re-litigates §6.9's WARNING rationale; belongs in its own plan). Simple-chore (docs only); should not block the rules plan.

chore.synopsis: Realign diagnostics spec §6.10's `extraction.placeholder_unfilled` rule expression operator

chores.chore: §6.10's YAML rule expression uses the regex-MATCH operator `=~` (anchored at position 0 in rule-engine 4.5.3), but the same section's test 4 requires regex-SEARCH semantics ("regex matches anywhere in the string"). The Cycle 1 integration fixture places the marker at position 0 of `statement_of_intent`, which masks the inconsistency at the integration level (the marker matches under either operator). Surfaced by reading library source during plan-review. The rules plan (plans index 8) deviates from the spec literal by emitting `=~~` (regex-search) in `builtin.yaml` to honor §6.10 test 4's documented semantics. Fix: amend §6.10's rule expression `=~` → `=~~`. Simple-chore (docs only); should land soon to keep spec and code aligned.

chore.synopsis: Cycle 4 evaluator code-quality cleanup: hoist `rule_engine` import in test, drop unused `pytest`, add dedicated test pinning the 3rd `EvaluationError` catch clause, and document the 4th `TypeError` workaround in the `evaluate()` docstring.

chores.chore: Surfaced during the code-quality review of plan 7 Task 4 (Cycle 4 — rule evaluator). Reviewer flagged one substantive coverage gap and several pure-polish nits; substantive ones bundled here. Substantive: `test_evaluator_eval_error_meta` actually exercises the 4th `except TypeError` clause (a defensive workaround for a rule-engine 4.5.3 truncation bug), not the 3rd `except EvaluationError` parent clause its name suggests — leaving an arm of the catch ladder untested. Fix: add `test_evaluator_evaluation_error_branch` using `trust.x / trust.y` with `y=0` to drive a bare `EvaluationError` through the 3rd clause. Polish bundled: hoist `rule_engine` import in the test (matches loader.py's module-level convention), drop unused `pytest` import, and document the 4th `TypeError` workaround in `evaluate()`'s docstring. Test-helper extraction (`_NOW`, `_make_ctx`, `_make_rule`) deferred to Cycle 5/6 once patterns repeat enough to justify a conftest fixture.

chore.synopsis: Realign diagnostics-engine-core plan-md with executed reality: pixi task args are positional (not key=value); BeneficiaryShare uses recipient_ref/share_percent (not beneficiary_name); Cycle 5 test 6 should match spec §6.6's atomic-write-per-line.

chores.chore: Surfaced during execution of plan 7 (`2026-04-23-diagnostics-engine-core`). The plan-md as committed at `6c3a8e8` carried three template stalenesses that misled subagent dispatches mid-session and required mid-flight corrections. Bundled here so a single fix-pass lands before the plan-md is referenced by future readers or replayed by automation. (1) Pixi task arguments are positional, not `name=value`. Multiple cycle templates wrote `pixi run test match=...` and `pixi run mypy target=...`; the correct form is `pixi run test test_eval_context` / `pixi run mypy v3/diagnostics`. The `name=value` form is silently treated as a literal positional and matches no tests, masking failures during dry runs. (2) `BeneficiaryShare` has no `beneficiary_name` field — the actual field is `recipient_ref`. The Cycle 2 template uses `beneficiary_name=`; the actually-landed test uses `recipient_ref` correctly, but the template was never reconciled. (3) Cycle 5 test 6 listed as `test_dir_creation_on_write`, but spec §6.6 mandates `test_atomic_write_per_line` (concurrent JSONL append exercising POSIX `O_APPEND` atomicity ≤ `PIPE_BUF`); spec §6.6 is authoritative. Simple-chore (docs only); should land before any future replay or external reference.

chore.synopsis: Tighten force_generation/validate_override_reason: document no-user-parameter security rationale + overridden_codes dedup contract; surface actual length in reason error; coerce whitespace-only file_number to 'unidentified'.

chores.chore: Surfaced during the cumulative final review of plan 7 (`2026-04-23-diagnostics-engine-core`). Cycle 6 landed `force_generation` and `validate_override_reason` with sufficient correctness for the public surface, but four small gaps remain — bundled here since all four sit inside `audit.py`. Docstring nits (no behavior change): document that `force_generation` deliberately accepts no `user:` parameter (the override identity comes from `config.user.upn`, not caller input — a security choice future maintainers might "fix"); document that `overridden_codes` performs no dedup (intentional — caller controls the diagnostic list). Behavior tweaks (need test coverage): surface the actual stripped length in `validate_override_reason`'s `ValueError` message; coerce whitespace-only `file_number` to `"unidentified"` (the current `or` short-circuit on Python falsiness lets `" "` pass through as a useless `trust_ref`). Code-chore; blast radius limited to `audit.py` + a `test_audit_log.py` extension. Pairs naturally with chore 9.

chore.synopsis: Add `__all__` declarations to v3/diagnostics submodules (audit, loader, engine, eval_context, errors) to harden public/private boundary; package __init__.py already declares one — submodules should match.

chores.chore: Surfaced during the cumulative final review of plan 7 (`2026-04-23-diagnostics-engine-core`). The package-level `__init__.py` declares an `__all__`, but the five submodules (`audit`, `loader`, `engine`, `eval_context`, `errors`) declare none — so `from ... import *` against any submodule pulls in private names alongside public ones, and static-analysis tools cannot identify private vs. public symbols at submodule granularity. Fix: add an `__all__` tuple to each submodule listing its intended public exports, keeping module-private helpers excluded. No symbol additions or renames. The package `__init__.py`'s `__all__` already constrains the public surface via re-exports; this chore is a defense-in-depth pass at submodule level. Code-chore but mechanical (no test changes); `pixi run check` should remain green.

chore.synopsis: Fix build_eval_context to unwrap str-mixin Enum to .value. rule-engine bypasses Python __eq__, so cycle-8 trust_type=='individual' fails despite str-mixin equality. Cycle 2 test pinned Python-side only; needs rule-engine roundtrip pin.

chores.chore: `build_eval_context` returns dicts containing raw Enum instances (Pydantic v2 `model_dump(mode="python")` does not unwrap them to their `.value`). For str-mixin enums like `TrustType(str, Enum)`, Python's inherited `__eq__` makes `TrustType.INDIVIDUAL == "individual"` return True — but rule-engine bypasses Python's `__eq__` and coerces via `str()`, which returns the enum repr (`"TrustType.INDIVIDUAL"`), not the value (`"individual"`). Rule expressions comparing enum-typed fields to string literals therefore silently return False. The diagnostics-engine spec (§5.2, §6.9 Refactor note) and the core-plan Cycle 2 `test_enum_value_pin` both assumed str-mixin equality would carry through rule-engine evaluation. The cycle-2 test pinned only Python-level equality (passes via str-mixin's inherited `__eq__`) and never asserted a rule-engine roundtrip, so the gap stayed latent until the first rule expression comparing an enum-typed field landed (cycle 8's `estate.crossed_cliff`, on `trust.trust_id.trust_type == "individual"`). Fix: add a recursive `_unwrap_enums()` helper in `eval_context.py` that replaces Enum instances with their `.value` (preserving Decimal/date/etc.); apply it to both `trust` and `firm` namespaces before return. Augment `test_enum_value_pin` with a rule-engine roundtrip assertion. Amend the spec (§5.2/§6.3/§6.9) and both plan-md files (core cycle 2; rules Task 2 Step 4 troubleshooting note) to describe the explicit unwrap mechanism instead of the incorrect str-mixin claim. Code-chore; blast radius is `eval_context.py` + 1 test augmentation + 3 doc files. Blocks resumption of plans index 8 cycle 8.

chore.synopsis: Realign diagnostics-engine-rules plan-md with executed reality: stale BeneficiaryShare field name, string-form integer Decimal literals, and missing loader-test collision callout in Task 1 Step 5.

chores.chore: Three template stalenesses in the rules plan-md required mid-flight corrections during execution of plans index 8 — same class of drift as chore 7 fixed in the core plan-md, inherited rather than learned from. Bundled here so one fix-pass lands before the plan-md is replayed or referenced. The drifts: (1) a stale `BeneficiaryShare` field name in Task 1+4 templates (model has no such field); (2) string-form `Decimal` literals for integer values that lint autofixes per project policy; (3) Task 1 Step 5's gate expectation missed a collision with three cycle-3 loader tests, requiring an unplanned monkeypatch deviation in the cycle 7 commit. Blast radius is the single rules plan-md file. Mirrors chore 7's pattern; should land before any future replay.

chore.synopsis: Add machine-readable `type` attribute (enum: code|simple) to the chore element in chores.xsd; backfill all existing chore entries with their classification derived from commit diff (closed) or body prose (open).

chores.chore: Surfaced during spec-pipeline skill design: the bare-slug resolver branch `query(chore scope touches code)?` requires a machine-readable type discriminator on the chore element, currently encoded only in body prose. Pre-flight amendment so the skill ships with a deterministic resolver from day one. Simple-chore — blast radius is the schema and the existing chore-attribute set in chores.xml; no `src/` or `tests/` scope.

chore.synopsis: Validate Qwen2.5-VL:7b vs MiniCPM-V on 10-20 firm-side handwritten intake samples; score per-field accuracy, illegibility precision/recall, hallucination rate; promote winner as default-recommended model in OllamaBackend docstring.

chores.chore: The OCR backend (spec §4.2) names Qwen2.5-VL:7b and MiniCPM-V as indicative model candidates based on third-party benchmark recon (DocVQA scores, handwriting/non-standard-font reputation), but the spec deliberately defers commitment to a specific model pending firm-side empirical evaluation. Generic benchmarks do not predict performance on this firm's handwriting distribution, fillable-form layout, or domain vocabulary, so the spec leaves `model=` as a constructor argument and treats the recommended default as evidence-gated. Method per spec §2 in-flight chore: collect 10-20 representative handwritten intake forms (consult paralegal staff on representativeness), run each through `OllamaBackend` configured for each candidate with `temperature=0`, score on per-field accuracy (matches paralegal-truth), illegibility-flag precision/recall, and hallucination rate (transcribed values for blank fields). Document findings in a separate session note; promote the winning model as the default-recommended `model=` argument in `OllamaBackend` documentation — do not hard-code (the constructor accepts model name as configuration). Initial corpus seeded during plan 9b spec-to-plan: a single-writer baseline corpus lives at `assets/handwriting-samples/`, partitioned into `pages/` (four full-payload narrative fixtures across writing techniques — see `pages/BASELINE.md`) and `snippets/` (five atomic single-purpose fixtures targeting §8.1/§8.3 disciplines with stratified oracle requirements — see `snippets/SNIPPETS.md`). The snippet corpus stratifies by oracle requirement (tier 1: absence-observable, ready for unattended automation; tier 2: paralegal-truth + unambiguous strokes, character-equality assertions; tier 3: paralegal-truth + spec-interpretation judgment, qualitative scoring) and is the recommended starting point for this chore's evaluation harness. The corpus is single-writer single-payload by construction; if the chore's exit criteria require more representative variability (e.g., neither candidate clears the usability bar), expand the corpus per the §4.2 firm-side-evaluation guidance before evaluating additional candidates. Exit criteria: documented model recommendation with sample-size-disclosed confidence; if neither candidate clears a usability bar (e.g., >85% per-field accuracy on legible fields), the chore extends to evaluating additional candidates (Llama 3.2-Vision is deprioritized per §4.2 single-source caveat). Blast radius is documentation only (plus expansion of `assets/handwriting-samples/` if the seeded corpus proves insufficient). Gated by completion of plan 9 cycle 5 (`OllamaBackend.extract` happy path) so the backend can actually be invoked against samples.

chore.synopsis: Add `test_envelope_complexity_ceiling.py` (pytest.mark.integration) characterizing pass-rate vs. envelope size on candidate vision models; opportunistically test reasoning-omission to gather §7.4 evidence. Informational, not gating.

chores.chore: Grammar-constrained decoding under llama.cpp (the mechanism Ollama inherits) can produce unexpected EOF errors or schema-violation retries when the constrained Pydantic schema grows beyond a model's effective complexity ceiling. Spec §7.5 plans for chunked extraction as a fallback strategy if the production envelope exceeds the ceiling on candidate vision models, but the threshold itself — in field count, JSON-schema bytes, or both — was unknown at the production envelope scale for Qwen2.5-VL:7b and MiniCPM-V. Method per spec §2 in-flight chore: added `test_envelope_complexity_ceiling.py` (pytest.mark.integration, opt-in) running `OllamaBackend.extract` against synthetic forms with controlled field counts, logging results to `tests/data/extraction_ceiling_log/`. Per-chore-body requirement: the persistence-in-code docstring blocks in `ollama_backend.py` and `trace.py` (the spec §2 "persistence in code" markers) were removed at fulfillment. Findings: qwen2.5vl:3b ceiling lies between 3 and 5 flat fields — 3-field cell passes at production scale (29s), 5-field cell entered non-terminating inference state (>20min), 10-field cell terminated with truncated JSON at 334s. Production `GenerationEnvelope` (3 top-level fields + nested $defs at 4085 bytes) is within the ceiling — §7.5 chunked-extraction trigger is NOT fired today. Output sequence length / constraint-grammar depth appears to be the operative factor; schema bytes alone don't predict. Three deferred items lifted into follow-up chores: qwen2.5vl:7b ceiling sweep (production-recommended model not yet measured), §7.4 reasoning-omission cells against qwen2.5vl:7b, and broader minicpm-v/gemma3 sweeps (lower priority). Full analysis at `docs/session-notes/2026-05-11-envelope-complexity-ceiling.md`.

chore.synopsis: Define canonical serialization for ExtractionTrace (recommendation: model_dump_json/model_validate_json round-trip with custom INCOMPLETE serializer/validator pair); choose persistence shape (sibling JSON vs embedded vs separate store).

chores.chore: v3.0 ships `ExtractionTrace` with in-memory-identity-only semantics for the `INCOMPLETE` sentinel — `model_dump_json()` round-trips will not preserve the sentinel because no custom serializer/validator pair is wired. This is intentional per spec §6.2: persistence questions belong to the consumer-layer (CLI/GUI) session that introduces a storage transport, not to the in-memory contract that this plan establishes. Method per spec §2 in-flight chore: when a consumer session lands trace persistence, define the canonical serialization shape. Recommendation (informational only; commitment lives in the consumer's session): adopt `model_dump_json()` / `model_validate_json()` as the canonical round-trip and ship a custom serializer/validator pair for `INCOMPLETE` (e.g., serialized as a tagged string and validated back to the sentinel via identity replacement). The same exercise resolves whether the trace persists alongside the trust as a sibling JSON, embedded in TrustData metadata, or in a separate store. Exit criteria: a brief design note documenting the chosen persistence shape, ratified by the consumer session that introduces it. Blast radius: design note plus the consumer session's storage layer plus a small `trace.py` patch wiring the custom INCOMPLETE serializer. Gated by a consumer-layer session for trust persistence existing — no plan currently scheduled, so this chore stays open until that work surfaces. Cross-references plans index 5 (shared-firm-config / SharePoint) as a candidate co-located transport.

chore.synopsis: Add `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` to pyproject.toml registering the `integration` marker and skipping it by default via `addopts = -m 'not integration'`; precondition for plan 9b task 9b-5 (live OCR smoke).

chores.chore: Plan 9b task 9b-5 introduces a live vision-model smoke test marked `pytest.mark.integration`, expected to be opt-in (skipped on `pixi run check`, run only when explicitly requested). The project currently has no pytest config: no `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` in pyproject.toml, no `pytest_addoption` in any conftest.py. Without this config, the `integration` marker is unregistered (pytest emits warnings when strict-markers is on, or treats the marker as a no-op tag) and the test runs by default on `pixi run check` — defeating the opt-in design and forcing every developer to have a live Ollama server running. Fix: add a `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` section to pyproject.toml with `markers = ["integration: live network/service tests, opt-in"]` and `addopts = "-m 'not integration'"`. The opt-in invocation becomes `pixi run test -m integration` (overrides the default-skip). The conftest.py-based `pytest_addoption` flag pattern is rejected as more ceremony than the declarative pyproject.toml approach for a single skip-by-default marker. Blast radius: pyproject.toml only (one section addition). Tests do not change. After this lands, plan 9b task 9b-5 is unblocked: its tests skip by default and run only via `pixi run test -m integration tests/v3/extraction/test_ollama_backend_integration.py`. Sibling chore #14 (envelope-complexity benchmark) also uses `pytest.mark.integration` and depends on this same config landing first.

chore.synopsis: GPU-accelerate the live OCR vision-model smoke. Resolved via IPEX-LLM Ollama drop-in: 104.08s vs 609.73s CPU baseline (5.87× speedup) on qwen2.5vl:7b after IGC version cleanup unblocked the SYCL JIT path.

chores.chore: Resolved 2026-04-29: IPEX-LLM Ollama works as a drop-in for upstream Ollama (HTTP-compatible at 127.0.0.1:11434, zero `src/` changes). Wall-clock 104.08s for the qwen2.5vl:7b OCR smoke vs. 609.73s CPU baseline = 5.87× speedup. Both assertions pass including the §7.4 grammar-constrained-decoding key-order pin. The original investigation had concluded the SYCL path was architecturally blocked under WSL2's MCDM SPIR-V→DXIL translator (RMS-Norm JIT failure) and recommended OpenVINO migration. **That diagnosis was wrong.** Actual root cause: stale `intel-igc-core 1.0.11378` packages in `/usr/local/lib` shadowed the proper `libigc1` from Intel's apt repo, breaking ALL OpenCL/SYCL kernel compilation. After purging the stale libs and installing the Debian-native compute-runtime stack, both OpenCL and SYCL JIT work correctly. Canonical correction lives in memory `project_wsl2_gpu_compute_dead_end.md` (revised 2026-04-29). IPEX-LLM bundle stays outside `src/` per the dev-tooling scope split: paralegals run AnthropicBackend in production; OllamaBackend is dev-only. Project-side residue limited to `0235eda` (pixi.toml env var unblocking the smoke test fixture path under the new working iGPU path). Polish chore #20 wraps the daemon swap as pixi tasks.

chore.synopsis: Apply A-7 to firm-config spec: append two-source loader contract from `2026-04-28-shared-firm-config-design.md` §9 into `2026-04-21-firm-config-design.md` post-finalization amendments. Pre-plan chore for indexes 5/12/13.

chores.chore: The `2026-04-28-shared-firm-config-design.md` spec restructures `load_firm_config` from single-file to two-source (shared + local) discovery and merge, replacing the loader's `path=` keyword with `local_path` + `shared_path` and introducing a SharePoint-hosted shared file with a sync-unavailability cache-fallback layer. §9 of that spec specifies the verbatim text of an amendment "A-7" to append to the predecessor firm-config spec, continuing the A-1 through A-6 series. §10 chore #1 of the new spec lists this amendment as a pre-planning prerequisite: it must land before plan composition references the firm-config spec as authoritative for the loader's pre-A-7 contract. Plans index 5/12/13 (foundation/cache/integration) all wait on this amendment before their `spec-to-plan` workflows can run cleanly. Blast radius: a single markdown file (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-21-firm-config-design.md`) with one section appended after A-6's "Confirmed" footer. No code, no tests, no schema. Verbatim §9 content carries one stale path reference (`2026-04-27-shared-firm-config-design` instead of the actual `2026-04-28-...md`) that the dispatch prompt instructs the executor to correct during paste.

chore.synopsis: Inline comment in `_resolve_fixture_path()` (test_ollama_backend_integration.py) claims `pixi run test` runs from the project root, but pixi.toml sets `cwd = 'tests/'` — the path-default fallback would resolve under `tests/assets/...` (nonexistent).

chores.chore: The `_resolve_fixture_path()` helper has two branches: read `OCR_SMOKE_FIXTURE_PATH` env var, or fall back to `Path("assets/handwriting-samples/pages/print.jpg")`. The fallback's inline comment claims "current working dir is the project root for `pixi run test`" — but `pixi.toml`'s test task sets `cwd = 'tests/'`, so the fallback would resolve under `tests/assets/...` (which doesn't exist) and the test would skip with "handwriting samples not found". Currently masked by `0235eda` adding `OCR_SMOKE_FIXTURE_PATH = '../assets/handwriting-samples/pages/print.jpg'` to the test task's env block — the env-path branch always fires under `pixi run test`, so the broken default never executes. The drift only manifests if a developer runs the test outside `pixi run test` (e.g., direct `pytest` invocation) without setting the env var. Fix shape: either correct the comment to reflect the actual `cwd = 'tests/'` (and the env-var-as-canonical-entry-point), or relocate the default to a repo-root-anchored path resolution (e.g., `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "assets/..."`). Blast radius: single function in one test file. Simple-chore (no behavior change either way for `pixi run test`).

chore.synopsis: Add pixi tasks wrapping the IPEX-LLM Ollama daemon swap (currently manual: kill upstream + nohup IPEX). Bundle is dev-tooling living outside `src/` at `/home/ramda/ipex-llm-ollama/...`; tasks should accept its location as a configurable input.

chores.chore: GPU-accelerated dev OCR currently requires manually swapping daemons: `kill <upstream-ollama-pid>` then `nohup /home/ramda/ipex-llm-ollama/ollama-ipex-llm-2.3.0b20250725-ubuntu/start-ollama-trustgen.sh > /tmp/ipex-ollama.log 2>&1 &`, with the reverse on swap-back. The sequence is documented in `/home/ramda/ipex-llm-ollama/GO.md` but not invocable from the project surface. Goal: add `pixi run ollama-gpu-start` and `pixi run ollama-gpu-stop` (or equivalent shape) that wrap the swap so `pixi run test -m integration` against the iGPU is a two-task sequence rather than ad-hoc shell. Constraint: the IPEX-LLM bundle path is dev-only (single-machine, version-specific by directory name `b20250725`), so the task must accept it as a configurable input — env var with a maintainer default, pixi `args` arg with a default, or per-machine override pattern. Hard-coding `/home/ramda/...` literally in the committed `pixi.toml` is rejected. Blast radius: pixi.toml only (two task additions plus any helper env-var declaration). No `src/` or `tests/` changes; the bundle and launcher script stay in their current dev-tooling location. Simple-chore. Gates nothing — current manual swap works.

chore.synopsis: Amend foundation plan-md `_EMPTY_LITERALS` prescription to subscripted `Final[tuple[str, dict[str, Any], list[Any]]]`; bare `Final = (...)` triggers mypy var-annotated on heterogeneous tuple.
chore.origin: Foundation plan execution mypy gate (cycle 1 Refactor)

chores.chore: The foundation plan-md (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-29-shared-firm-config-foundation.md`) prescribes the Cycle 1 Refactor stage to introduce `_EMPTY_LITERALS: Final = ("", {}, [])` as a module-level constant for the `_is_empty()` membership check. The bare `Final = (...)` annotation form was carried verbatim into the prescribed code block at line 206 of the plan-md. Mypy 1.x rejects this annotation under `[var-annotated]`: PEP 591 requires bare `Final` to have a single inferable literal type, and the heterogeneous tuple `(str, dict, list)` cannot collapse to one. The Cycle 1 Refactor commit failed the `pixi run check` gate during foundation execution until a follow-up annotation correction (`Final[tuple[str, dict[str, Any], list[Any]]]`) was squashed in. The corrected annotation is now in v3.0.0's Cycle 1 Refactor commit; the plan-md still carries the original (rejected) shape for any future re-execution. Blast radius: a single line in a single markdown file (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-29-shared-firm-config-foundation.md`). Simple-chore. Gates nothing — the source code is correct on v3.0.0. The current `firm.py` omits the call, leaving the spec-prescribed bridge unwired. The drift is functionally invisible today because no subscriber exists yet. It manifests when the diagnostics-engine warning-subscriber plan lands: the subscriber would either need to import firm.py defensively to opportunistically trigger a `captureWarnings` call, or fall back to a `warnings.showwarning` override — neither honors the spec's one-shot import-time bridging design, and both push subscription-timing concerns into the consumer. Resolve in one of two directions: (a) add the call to firm.py at module-import time — matches spec verbatim, single-line blast radius; (b) amend §5.5.5.5 to document the showwarning-override mechanism as the actual subscription path — preserves current code, spec-only blast radius. Blocks the future diagnostics-engine warning-subscriber chore.

chore.synopsis: Gemma3 vision rejection root-caused: SYCL0 worst-case-graph OOM in `multimodalStore.getTensor` under IPEX-LLM Ollama 0.9 fork, not a text-only build. Two alt architectures (moondream, llava-llama3) eval'd and rejected. qwen2.5vl:7b stands.

chores.chore:
Initial hypothesis (that the `gemma3:12b` Ollama tag was text-only) was wrong. Re-pulling both `gemma3:4b` and `gemma3:12b` confirmed `capabilities: ['completion', 'vision']` with mmproj projector tensors. The runner still terminates with `exit status 2` at ~2-4s per request. Server-side journal capture revealed the actual failure: a panic in `multimodalStore.getTensor` at `multimodal.go:98`, called from `reserveWorstCaseGraph` — the 1.39GB projector tensor (slot #35) plus 34 per-layer weight allocations exceed the IPEX-LLM SYCL0 budget on the Iris Xe iGPU. Same constraint family as chore #30 (SYCL0 buffer allocation), different boundary. Compounded by IPEX-LLM Ollama being pinned to upstream Ollama 0.9, which predates most multimodal allocator improvements; Gemma3 vision support is mostly post-0.9. Pivoted per chore exit criteria to evaluate alternative architecture classes. `moondream:1B` (Phi-2 base) runs cleanly but scored 0.8% MATCH with 82 hallucinations on the §8.3 absent-fields fixture alone — most paralegal-hostile failure mode observed. `llava-llama3:8b` (LLaVA CLIP-ViT-L + Llama3 backbone, size-matched to qwen2.5vl:7b) scored 5.9% MATCH with honest-OMIT failure pattern (refuses on hard fixtures rather than hallucinating) but still unusable accuracy. Five architecture families now tested across chores #13 + #29 + #33: Qwen2.5-VL, Qwen2-based (minicpm-v), LLaVA-Llama3, Phi-2-based (moondream), Gemma3 (SigLIP+Gemma3). Two are production-grade-or-baseline; three are not viable; Gemma3 is infrastructure-gated (would need re-test if IPEX-LLM rebases on newer upstream). Closing disposition: qwen2.5vl:7b recommendation reaffirmed across three evaluation rounds. Production code path unchanged. Session-note addendum at `docs/session-notes/2026-04-30-vision-model-eval.md` captures the runner-panic trace inline + per-fixture detail for all three candidates. Re-opening this chore should be triggered only by an IPEX-LLM Ollama version bump past 0.10, or by access to a system with discrete GPU (Iris Xe SYCL0 budget is the structural ceiling here).
Post-close amendment (2026-05-13 PM): two additional candidates evaluated under a 10-min total-eval disqualifier rule. `granite3.2-vision:2b` produced the strongest quality finding of the entire sweep — 55.9% MATCH with zero HALLUCINATIONs (paralegal-triage safer than qwen2.5vl:3b's 48.9% MATCH with 4 hallucinations) — but disqualified on wall-clock (17:56 + 600s timeout on `pages/hurried.jpg`). `llava:7b` ran 17min before kill; smoke test confirmed normal chat-mode behavior (~6-34s, correct content). Both candidates expose the same structural finding: Ollama 0.9's grammar-constrained sampler, combined with spec §7.3's `format=GenerationEnvelope.model_json_schema()` pin, penalizes models without document-structured pretraining — token re-sampling on grammar-disallowed tokens explodes wall-clock. Qwen2.5-VL aligns naturally with the grammar; LLaVA / Granite / Gemma3 do not. Reaffirms the qwen2.5vl:7b recommendation across four evaluation rounds and six architecture families. Re-opening gated on IPEX-LLM Ollama version bump past 0.10 (where upstream improved both multimodal allocation and grammar-constrained sampling); relaxing `format=...` is not on the table (breaks spec §7.3 schema-pin guarantee).
Follow-up amendment (2026-05-13 PM, after granite/llava): re-pulled `moondream:1B` and applied the smoke-test diagnostic lens. Probe-1 ("describe this image") returned 54 tokens correctly identifying the grantor name; probe-2 ("yes/no") and probe-3 (`/api/generate`) returned `eval_count=1` — moondream emits EOS immediately for non-captioning prompts. Moondream is a captioning model, not an extraction model. This reframes the original 0.8% MATCH / 82-hallucination result: NOT a model-capability failure; the runner forced moondream past its EOS prior under grammar pressure, and re-sampling produced a flat distribution over schema-allowed tokens that flowed random names from pretraining into structurally-valid JSON slots. Adds a second grammar-constrained-decoding failure mode to the diagnostic taxonomy alongside the re-sample slowdown observed on LLaVA/Granite. Both reduce to the same root cause (token distribution mis-aligned with the grammar lattice); qwen2.5vl:7b's document-structured pretraining avoids both. Recommendation unchanged.
Final follow-up (2026-05-13 PM): two open questions answered. (1) Per-fixture timing variance is a fingerprint of grammar-mismatch failure mode — granite 1.6× (tight, schema-lattice traversal dominates), llava-llama3 3.6× (moderate, OMIT-vs-extract mix), moondream 13.9× (wild, EOS-flood depth). (2) Granite re-probe on `pages/hurried.jpg` in chat-mode terminated in 31.6s with content "unanswerable" (eval_count=5). The harness 600s timeout was misattributed — it was granite trying to refuse under a JSON-schema grammar that has no refusal path. Discovered third grammar-constrained-decoding failure mode: **refusal-vs-schema collision** (qwen2.5vl:3b's runner-stops on illegibility-stress.jpg is plausibly the same mechanism). Reclassified granite's MISMATCH verdicts: content-correct rate is 69.7% (vs 55.9% strict-MATCH) — within 7-8pp of qwen2.5vl:7b. Granite wall-clock decomposes cleanly: ~8min successful + 10min refusal-collision; without collision overhead the eval fits within the 10-min budget. **Granite is salvageable conditional on harness changes** (detect grammar-stuck state, schema-relaxation for refusal, or per-fixture short-timeout-with-retry) — not in scope for chore #33. qwen2.5vl:7b recommendation unchanged for current code path.
Honest retest (2026-05-13 PM): user correctly identified the prior DQ as lazy — wall-clock was measured under a known-incompatible invocation pattern without testing whether transitioning to a corrected pattern resolves it. Ran the retest using only the `prompt_builder=` public seam (no schema or backend changes) + 120s per-request ceiling. Refusal-targeted prompt resolved hurried.jpg from 600s timeout → 59.1s clean envelope with `{"reasoning":"...mark each field as illegible...","grantors":[{},{}], "beneficiaries":[{},{}]}`. Full eval: **9:35 total — UNDER the 10-min budget**. But accuracy regressed (44.1% strict MATCH vs 55.9% production-prompt) with **1 new HALLUCINATION** on absent-fields.jpg and over-refusal on legible fixtures (all-caps -5 MATCH, label-on-line -1). Three honest revisions: (a) "DQ on wall-clock" was lazy, granite is NOT structurally disqualified; (b) neither granite configuration is strictly better than qwen2.5vl:7b — both dominated on the accuracy/wall-clock Pareto frontier (7b: 77.1% at ~6min); (c) granite's distinguishing feature is the safety profile (0 invented content) preserved ONLY under the production prompt — the refusal-prompt sacrifices it. Granite remains a documented backup candidate, not a replacement. Re-opening criteria sharpened: Ollama 0.10+ rebase OR prompt-engineering investment preserving §8.3 guardrails while enabling refusal — neither in scope. Production code path unchanged.
